remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was made before launch for the named small-business onboarding use case.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance covering the segment gap before launch.
The small-business onboarding segment misses target by 1.3 percentage points and is named in two paid pilot commitments, which meets the stated materiality rule on this record.
Legal review remains open, so the policy predicate is unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness context but do not satisfy the specific disclosure or risk-acceptance requirement.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a more caveated interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more careful, but it does not resolve the controlling compliance predicate. Under the stated policy, a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the record shows a 1.3-point miss in a segment named in two paid pilot commitments with legal review still open. The Actor also concedes that the present record does not show disclosure or approved risk acceptance. That means the case may support a statement that overall technical readiness evidence exists, but it still does not support a compliant certification finding on the present record. Caveated packaging is not enough where the unresolved caveat is itself a required pre-launch compliance condition.
